annotations.description: The CSI node plugin's own ceiling-backed-v1 check failed: the pool's committed ceilings plus unattributed mappings exceed what it can back after its reserve, data or metadata entered the reserve, or the pool left its qualified state. Full data alone is normal: every volume is fully backed and caches fill their ceilings, so this rule, not data used over pool size, is the signal that tenant writes can run the pool out of space. The node admits no new volumes meanwhile. Read /v1/node on the node's allocator socket for the reason, committed_bytes, usable_bytes and unattributed_mapped_bytes, and reclaim unattributed mappings or move volumes through the planned migration path. Never extend or convert the pool by hand as a fix.
annotations.summary: Kura thin pool {{ $labels.vg }}/{{ $labels.pool }} on {{ $labels.node }} ({{ $labels.cluster }}) cannot back its volumes

model.expr: max by (cluster, node, vg, pool) (1 - kura_volumes_thin_pool_healthy)

title: Kura thin pool cannot back its volumes

annotations.description: Thin pool metadata exhaustion is worse than data exhaustion: the pool goes read-only or fails and needs an offline thin_check. The conservative profile sizes metadata at 128 bytes per chunk, 1 MiB per device slot and a reserve, so growth past this level means more devices than planned or snapshots. Stop new placements on the node and inspect lvs -a before metadata runs out. Never run thin_check against the live metadata device.
annotations.summary: Kura thin pool {{ $labels.vg }}/{{ $labels.pool }} on {{ $labels.node }} ({{ $labels.cluster }}) metadata is {{ $values.A.Value | humanizePercentage }} used

model.expr: max by (cluster, node, vg, pool) (kura_volumes_thin_pool_metadata_used_bytes) / max by (cluster, node, vg, pool) (kura_volumes_thin_pool_metadata_size_bytes)

title: Kura thin pool metadata usage high

title: Kura thin pool metadata almost full

annotations.description: device-mapper reports the pool as out_of_data_space, read-only, needs_check or failed. Tenant writes on every thin volume of this node fail now. Check dmsetup status and the kernel log on the node, keep every volume, and move instances off the node through the planned migration path. Do not run thin_check or lvconvert --repair against an active pool.
annotations.summary: Kura thin pool {{ $labels.vg }}/{{ $labels.pool }} on {{ $labels.node }} ({{ $labels.cluster }}) is read-only or out of data space

model.expr:
max by (cluster, node, vg, pool) (
  label_replace(kura_volumes_thin_pool_read_only, "condition", "read_only", "", "")
  or label_replace(kura_volumes_thin_pool_out_of_data_space, "condition", "out_of_data_space", "", "")
)

title: Kura thin pool read-only or out of data space

annotations.description: A node labelled tuist.dev/kura-thin-ready=true has published no fresh pool observation for 15 minutes. Either its CSI plugin is down or not scraped, or the plugin's observations fail, which also withdraws the node's tuist.dev/kura-disk capacity. The usage alerts are blind for this node until it recovers. Read the driver container's logs for the observation error and check the pod's scrape target.
annotations.summary: Kura thin pool metrics are missing on {{ $labels.node }} ({{ $labels.cluster }})

model.expr: max by (cluster, node) (kube_node_labels{label_tuist_dev_kura_thin_ready="true"}) unless on (cluster, node) ((max by (cluster, node) (kura_volumes_thin_pool_data_size_bytes) and on (cluster, node) (max by (cluster, node) (time() - kura_volumes_thin_pool_last_observation_timestamp_seconds) < 600)) or (max by (cluster, node) (kube_node_labels{label_tuist_dev_kura_thin_ready="true"}) < -1))
